steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease two 9x5 inch loaf pans.

In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, salt, baking soda, sugar and cinnamon. Add the walnuts, eggs, oil, banana, pineapple, vanilla, coconut and cherries; stir just until blended. Pour batter evenly into the prepared pans.

Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 60 minutes, or until a tooth pick inserted into the center of a loaf comes out clean. Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then remove to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Hawaiian Banana Nut Bread
raw_recipe.description: This is a recipe that I put together, out of several different ones. It's very easy and very good.

review.reviewBody:
EVERYONE loved this!! From my picky husband and 4 year old son, to all my guests on Easter day. Have made it twice in the last week! Using advice from another reviewer, I didn't change a thing the first time and it was perfect. The second time, I tried it without the coconut. It is much better with the coconut IMHO! Also, 2 cups of bananas is 4 average-size bananas. This should help so you're not having to measure your bananas after they're mashed. I usually have a hard time not making my own little changes to a recipe...which is why I tried to change it the second time. Don't change a thing! This recipe is going to be my Christmas neighbor-gifts for next year! Very colorful and easy to make. Thanks for sharing a great recipe!
P.S. Added on 8/24/07, I have now made this recipe MANY times and here are a few more helpful tips (hopefully). First, this recipe will fill three of the aluminum loaf pans that you can purchase for gift giving. Also, the last time I made this I added ALOT of pineapple. That is a big mistake! It makes the bread too gooey, so if you experiment, this is not the ingredient to increase. And one last thing. At least when I bake this, it takes around 55 minutes to be done, at least. My oven is right on, temperature wise, too. ENJOY!!

Well deserved rating!! I followed the suggestions and only used 1/2 cup of vegetable oil and replaced the other half with unsweetened apple sauce to cut the fat. I also substituted 1 cup of white sugar for brown sugar. Lastly, I only used 1/2 cup of cocoa nut flakes, which was coco-nutty enough. It would’ve been too fibrous otherwise. Do NOT add more or less fruit, everything as is has the perfect balance. I would add a light glaze for presentation.

The first time we made it, we made four loaves for a church function which requested no nuts. Also didn't have the cherries on hand and no time to get them. WITHOUT the walnuts and cherries this was a TOTAL hit. People raved about it. Then we made two loaves following the recipe with walnuts and cherries. Another total hit! I've had a lot of banana bread over the years but this is just FANTASTIC. A keeper for me. Thank you Saundra for posting this recipe. Note: We think our oven is possessed. First time cooked it for the full 60 minutes using dark pans and the bottom come out a touch too dark. Second time used "convection bake" and took it out 5 minutes early, probably should have left it in for the full 60 minute. Basically just watch it the last ten minutes... You won't be disappointed. PS: I'm not a fan of maraschino cherries in general but won't ever make this w/o them again.

Yes I made some changes. I hate coconut so I used shredded carrots instead. I felt that Maraschino cherries would be to strong so I substituted 1/2 a 16oz can of cherry pie filling. It turned out awesome. Next time I’m gonna use more cherry pie filling or apples instead. 

Great recipe. I’m claiming it as mine. Lol.

I am making this for 2 friends of mine that are not able to do butter or too much suger. I used coconut oil, maple syrup instead of sugar and dates instead of the cherry. Maple syrup I did 1 cup instead of 2, I did half of a 15oz pinapple drained and added a little more flour to this. Omg...sooooo good. In my opinion it is sweet enough but since I am European I like it less sweet. Thing of taste I guess. Thank u for this recipe!

I didn’t put the cherries in it, and used pecans instead, added some clove and nutmeg as well. Also, when the loaves were hot out of the oven I used to leftover pineapple juice to pour over the top to moisten the top of the loaves. It was incredibly good! Overall the recipe cooked well and I enjoyed it!

Used 1 1/2 cup of sugar because bananas were very ripe. The ripper they are the sweeter. 
Very good everyone loved. Made these for Christmas gifts.
I made this and everyone loved it. I did only use 1 cup of sugar instead of 2.
The only thing I did different was to roast the nuts and coconut before adding them. This by far was the best version of banana bread I have ever made.

I've made this Hawaiian banana bread many, many times because it's the most delicious banana bread I've ever made. I leave the cherries out, but that's the only thing I do differently. Thank you for such a delicious recipe!

Fantastic Recipe!!!! I used coconut oil instead if vegetable oil and dried bing cherries instead of maraschino. Reduced cooking time to 50 minutes. Grease the pan very well, mine stuck a bit. I can’t wait to make it again with maraschino cherries. Definitely my new favorite banana bread!!!
I've been making this recipe for years, and everyone loves it. However, I've always omitted the cherries and coconut, because I don't like either! Delicious!!!
I make it often for my neighbors and for work, I usually double the recipe and cut the marichinos in half and add a cup of mini chocolate chips.. It is amazing

Excellent recipe. I added semi sweet chocolate morsels instead of the maraschino cherries and used pecans instead of walnuts. I made a pineapple glaze using some of the leftover pineapple juice, coconut extract and some confectioners sugar. Yummy!! Thank you for this delicious recipe. I’ll never make banana bread without pineapple and coconut again!
It was great I used half brown sugar half white and fresh pineapple chunks and olive oil and butter1/2 in 1/2
Great recipe that levels up basic banana bread.

I didn't like it as much as I thought I would. I halved the recipe, I followed directions and made no substitutions. The bread baked nicely but to me, the flavors got lost in the mix, instead of enhancing one another. I couldn't taste the banana, nor the cherries. Personal preference, I think, because I gave some of the bread to my neighbor and she liked it.
Family and neighbors really liked this recipe.

My aim was 4 LG loaf pans, I used 2 C crushed fresh pineapple, untrained, 2 mashed C bananas, 2 C fresh blueberries, 2 scant C chopped pecans, used 4 eggs, 1 C. oil, and 1/3 C. melted butter, 2 C white sugar and 1/2 C. brown sugar, added orange and lemon extract to taste, on dry ingredients I used 1/3 more than called for, added 1 t. baking powder, omitted coconut and cherries due to blueberries
Made this and added some nutmeg per a suggestion, but it was still missing something. If I made this again I’d add orange zest
